name: rea-video
description: Analyze video shots and export a timing and production breakdown in VIDEO.md.
installation: Agent plugin or documented Python CLI setup
tradeoff: Offline analysis is documented. Optional model-assisted analysis has separate requirements.
licenseTerms: Apache-2.0 for repository code. Review rights for source footage, music and likenesses before reuse.

name: Awesome Opus 5.5 Videos
description: Browse examples of AI-made videos with links to creator posts and shared prompts.
installation: Browse the repository or linked gallery
tradeoff: Use examples for reference. Check permission before reusing a creator’s assets or prompts.
licenseTerms: The repository declares MIT. Source videos, prompts and linked works retain their respective rights.

name: Lemo-Opuscar
description: Create code-rendered films with an agent skill and a library of style examples.
installation: Reviewed Claude Code plugin or manual skill installation
tradeoff: Review per-file terms and exclude third-party media and narration from reuse unless cleared.
licenseTerms: Code is MIT. Style documents are CC BY-NC 4.0 with additional permissions for film production. Licensable demo materials are CC BY 4.0, subject to listed exclusions.

name: EffectCraft
description: Compose motion graphics, edit layered timelines and render projects from a Rust desktop app or CLI.
installation: Platform binary or Cargo source build
permissions: Can edit project data and write rendered output
tradeoff: Headless MCP exposes supported engine commands. Desktop bridge capabilities depend on the running application.
licenseTerms: The project offers a choice of MIT or Apache-2.0. Review notices for bundled dependencies and assets.

name: pixelfx
description: Render procedural pixel-art effects in JavaScript or export animation sprite sheets.
installation: Review the repository-backed npm package or use its documented source modules
tradeoff: The optional Patch publishing flow requires Patch Desktop on Windows. The browser library runs independently.
licenseTerms: MIT covers repository code subject to its notice requirements. Check rights for assets added to your own project.

name: ComfyUI
description: Run node-based generative workflows locally or through Comfy’s developer platform.
dependencies: Python and a supported inference backend for manual setup
installation: Desktop installer on macOS or Windows, or documented manual setup
permissions: Custom nodes run code with the process’s permissions
tradeoff: Local generation depends on hardware and model support. Cloud services and partner API nodes can incur fees.
licenseTerms: GPL version 3 for ComfyUI. Verify separate licenses for model weights, custom nodes and hosted APIs.

name: Remotion
description: Create React video compositions and render them with the Remotion CLI or Node.js API.
installation: Create a project using the official Remotion scaffolder
integrations: Browser WebMCP for supported browser workflows
tradeoff: The hosted documentation MCP was shut down. Team eligibility and hosted rendering costs vary.
licenseTerms: Remotion grants free use to eligible individuals and companies of up to three people. Other organizations need the applicable company license. Check the terms for your version.

name: Remotion Agent Skills
description: Add Remotion authoring and rendering guidance to Codex and other compatible coding agents.
dependencies: Remotion project for project-specific authoring and rendering
installation: Use the documented Remotion, skills CLI or GitHub CLI installation flow
tradeoff: The skills guide a coding agent. Running and licensing the renderer requires a separate Remotion setup.
licenseTerms: No standalone repository license or license files were verified. Consult upstream before redistribution. Remotion’s product license applies separately.

name: HyperFrames
description: Create and render editable video compositions with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and an agent-assisted workflow.
installation: Review the local HyperFrames CLI or Studio installer before use
tradeoff: The local renderer has a no-paid-API path. The hosted connector requires eligible accounts and has separate costs.
licenseTerms: Apache-2.0 covers the open repository. Hosted connector, paid Studio features, media and model providers have separate terms.

name: three.js
description: Build animated 3D scenes and render them in compatible browsers with JavaScript.
dependencies: WebGL or WebGPU-capable browser for the selected renderer
installation: Install the three package or use its documented browser module setup
tradeoff: three.js renders scenes. A separate capture and encoding stage produces a video file.
licenseTerms: MIT covers the library. Review separate terms for imported 3D models, textures and fonts.

name: GSAP
description: Animate UI and scene properties with JavaScript timelines, easing and plugins.
installation: Install the gsap npm package or use a documented script build
tradeoff: An animation library. Rendering and encoding final media require separate tooling.
licenseTerms: The GSAP Standard License permits many uses without a fee and imposes restrictions, including on certain competing products. Review the current terms before integration or redistribution.

name: MCP for Blender
description: Connect an MCP client to the community Blender add-on for scene inspection and editing.
installation: Review and install the add-on and configure the MCP client manually
permissions: Can modify Blender scenes and run Python with Blender permissions
tradeoff: Use an isolated workspace and only grant access to intended projects. Optional asset or AI integrations require separate review.
licenseTerms: MIT covers this community integration. Blender, imported assets and optional external services have separate terms.

name: FFmpeg
description: Inspect, transcode, filter and assemble video or audio using command-line tools and C libraries.
dependencies: An FFmpeg build with the required encoders and filters
installation: Use a trusted platform package or build the required configuration from source
tradeoff: GitHub is the project mirror. Codec availability and redistribution obligations depend on how the binary was built.
licenseTerms: The default project baseline is LGPL-2.1-or-later. Optional GPL components or external libraries can change build terms. Nonfree builds can be nonredistributable. Check codecs and patent obligations.
